turns.answer:
**Needs information**

Your pension is governed by Article 12, but no pension figure can be given until your fund corrects your record from Article 11 to Article 12. Your salary, service, and averages currently on file are administered under the other Article and are not the right basis here.

You have confirmed that you are an employee of a board of park commissioners. Article 12 covers employees of such a board, subject to the Code’s listed exceptions. [40 ILCS 5/12-118]

For a withdrawal on or after December 31, 2003, Article 12 provides a fixed-benefit annuity of 2.40% for each year of credited service, based on the highest average annual salary for any 4 consecutive years within the last 10 years of service. The annuity is capped at 80% of that average salary. If retirement is before age 60, the Code generally provides a reduction of 1/4 of 1% for each month or fraction before age 60, unless you have at least 30 years of service. [40 ILCS 5/12-133]

The earlier fixed-benefit rates apply only to withdrawals before December 31, 2003, so they do not apply to the provision being considered. The accumulation-based provisions in Sections 12-133(b) and 12-130 apply only to employees who entered service before July 1, 1971, so they do not apply to the provision being considered. [40 ILCS 5/12-133] [40 ILCS 5/12-130]

Please have your fund first confirm that Article 12 is your correct coverage. After that, what was your age at withdrawal from service, how many years of service you have with the fund, and what was your salary for each of the last ten years, or your best four consecutive years? Those details are needed for the age eligibility, service amount, salary average, and any reduction before age 60.

turns.question: What does Section 11-134 say about the annuity formula?
turns.answer:
Section 11-134 provides several annuity formulas. For qualifying employees with at least 20 years of service, the formula generally uses a stated percentage for each year of service and the highest average annual salary over 4 consecutive years within the last 10 years before withdrawal. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

- The formula includes different rates for different blocks of service. One elected formula uses 2.40% for each year of service when withdrawal is on or after January 1, 2002.
- The annuity generally begins no earlier than age 55, or age 50 for an employee with at least 30 years of service under one provision. An annuity beginning before age 60 may be reduced by 0.25% for each full month or remaining fractional part before age 60, unless an exception applies. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]
- An employee with at least 20 years of service may elect among certain formulas in Section 11-134. The Code also sets maximum percentages of highest average annual salary, including an 80% maximum for withdrawals on or after January 1, 2002. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]
- Section 11-134(f-1) provides another election for an employee with at least 10 years of service. It begins no earlier than age 60 and uses the applicable percentage for each year of service, subject to the stated maximum. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]
- To work out a dollar amount, the applicable withdrawal date, your elected formula, and whether any early-retirement exception applies would need to be established. The salary and service figures alone do not select among the formulas.

turns.question: What retirement annuity does Article 8 provide for a police officer with 25 years?
turns.answer:
Article 8 does not provide one fixed retirement annuity solely because a police officer has 25 years of service. The amount depends on the Article 8 formula and the member’s applicable salary and retirement details.

- A police officer’s service is counted as city employee service under Article 8. Post-effective-date service counts only if the required contributions are paid and the same service is not retained in another pension fund. [40 ILCS 5/8-227]
- Article 8 limits an age-and-service annuity to no more than 60% of the employee’s highest salary, subject to the statutory exceptions for automatic increases. [40 ILCS 5/8-154]
- The law also provides an early-retirement incentive, but only for employees who met its specific 2003–2004 eligibility and election requirements. [40 ILCS 5/8-138.4]
- This member’s own pension is under Article 11, not Article 8. To work out an Article 8 amount, the applicable Article 8 annuity formula and the police officer’s highest salary would be needed.
